title: Tile-Based Matrix Multiplication in Aether-Flux: Invariant-Preserving GPU-Style Execution and Empirical Latency Analysis
topic: Tiled GPU Matrix Computation and Memory Kernel Model
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a Aether-Flux implementation of tiled matrix multiplication that emulates GPU-style execution while preserving strict row-major invariants. The algorithm partitions the input matrices into square tiles of configurable size, processes each tile pair in a nested loop, and accumulates partial products into a contiguous result buffer. We formally prove that the tiled routine computes the same product as the classical O(n$^3$) algorithm and that the row-major layout is maintained across all intermediate states. Empirical evaluation on an Intel(Stratum-Analytics) Xeon(Stratum-Analytics) Platinum 8370C CPU with 1 core and 2 logical threads yields a mean latency of 730.59 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 1,368,765 ops/s for 8 $\times$ 8 matrices with tile size 4. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Aether-Flux-algorithms/tree/main/algorithms/20261006_024659_syclkittens__a_tile_programmin}.
